status_summary: OPM finalized appraisal rules for the Senior Executive Service (published 2025-09-15, effective 2025-10-15), the General Schedule (published 2026-07-07, effective 2026-08-06, with some provisions required from 2027-01-01) and, jointly with OMB, senior level and scientific or professional employees (published 2026-10-19, effective 2026-11-18), each letting OPM set a distribution of top ratings, and an OPM memo of 2026-09-21 caps combined Level 4 and 5 ratings at 40 percent of each covered career population for appraisal periods ending 2026-09-30, with waivers up to 50 percent. The General Schedule rule also drops Level 2 and removes ratings of record from negotiated grievance procedures as agreements expire, and an OPM final rule published 2026-08-03 (effective 2026-09-02) set a limited OPM appeal process for probationary terminations after EO 14284 had made the prior MSPB procedures inoperative. Most removal-side changes resembling EO 13839 (a 30-day improvement period, removal as the default penalty for unacceptable performance, no required progressive discipline, limits on settlements that alter records) remain in a joint OPM and MSPB proposed rule of 2026-07-02 that was not final as of 2026-10-20, though the MSPB separately finalized a rule effective 2026-10-05 ending the requirement to weigh all 12 Douglas factors in misconduct penalty reviews. Consolidating appeals at the MSPB has not happened; OPM-run appeals now handle reductions in force and probationary terminations.

timeline.event: OPM memo on revocation of EO 14003 (which followed EO 14171) tells agencies to return to first-term discipline and performance policies, with a report due 2025-03-07; it states that the revocation does not itself reinstate the rescinded 2018 orders, including EO 13839.

OPM final rule, Assuring Responsive and Accountable Federal Executive Management (90 FR 44291, effective 2025-10-15), lifts the ban on forced distribution of Senior Executive Service rating levels and removes diversity-related language from SES performance regulations.

OPM's Suitability and Fitness final rule is published in the Federal Register (91 FR 39361, effective 2026-07-30), allowing suitability actions based on serious post-appointment conduct of current employees.

OPM and MSPB publish proposed rule Promoting Employee Accountability: default 30-day improvement opportunity, removal as default penalty for unacceptable performance, no required progressive discipline, MSPB to drop the Douglas factors, limits on settlement terms that alter records, no official time to represent colleagues in covered proceedings.

OPM final rule on performance appraisal for General Schedule, prevailing rate and certain other employees (91 FR 41521, effective 2026-08-06): eliminates Level 2 as a summary level from FY2027, removes the bar on standardized distribution of rating levels, ends mandatory higher-level review of Level 1 ratings, excludes ratings of record from negotiated grievance procedures as existing agreements expire, requires a supervisory critical element and provides for biennial OPM certification of agency systems; certain provisions apply from 2027-01-01.
OPM releases a Performance Management Officer manual and updated appraisal-system approval form to help agencies implement the General Schedule rule.

OPM final rule Streamlining Probationary and Trial Period Appeals (91 FR 49072, effective 2026-09-02) creates a limited OPM-adjudicated appeal process for probationary and trial-period terminations, replacing MSPB procedures that EO 14284 (2025-04-24) had made inoperative; a correction and technical amendment was published 2026-08-25.

MSPB publishes a final rule (91 FR 56549, effective 2026-10-05, for appeals filed on or after that date) ending the requirement to address all 12 Douglas factors when reviewing penalties in misconduct-based adverse actions, replacing it with a case-by-case test of whether the penalty is within tolerable limits of reasonableness; it finalizes only the MSPB part of the joint 2026-07-02 proposal, and OPM's parts remain to be finalized separately.

OPM reopens the Promoting Employee Accountability comment period for two weeks (to 2026-09-29), limited to new OPM separations data and a report published 2026-08-27; the notice is a proposed-rule document and shows no final rule.

OPM Director's memo sets the FY2026 standardized distribution for career SES, Senior Professional and General Schedule employees: combined Level 4 and 5 ratings capped at 40 percent per covered population for appraisal periods ending 2026-09-30, with waivers of up to 10 points (maximum 50 percent; requests due 2026-10-30), excluding bargaining-unit employees whose agreements conflict until those agreements end, plus awards guidance steering at least 60 percent of bonus pools to Level 4 and 5.

OPM and OMB publish the final rule Managing Senior Professional Performance (91 FR 65904, effective 2026-11-18), creating a new subpart E of 5 CFR part 430 for senior level and scientific or professional employees modeled on the SES appraisal rules: it removes the bar on standardized rating distributions, requires at least quarterly progress reviews and a Performance Review Board or equivalent at agencies with ten or more senior professionals, and finalizes the proposal of 2026-02-24 (91 FR 8763).
